q: What does the BRSR question 'do your policies extend to value chain partners' mean for suppliers?
title: BRSR: do your policies cover suppliers?
short: Section B question 3 asks a listed company, for each of the nine principles, whether its policies extend to value chain partners: yes or no. Question 4 asks which codes and certifications it has adopted under each principle. For a supplier, a yes means a code of conduct to sign and evidence to show.
audience: MSME suppliers asked to sign a listed buyer's supplier code of conduct

ul: Question 3: Do the enlisted policies extend to your value chain partners? Yes or no, for each of Principles 1 to 9.

Question 4: Name the national and international codes, certifications, labels or standards adopted, under each principle. SEBI's examples: Forest Stewardship Council, Fairtrade, Rainforest Alliance, Trustea, SA 8000, OHSAS, ISO and BIS.

sections.h: What a yes means for you
ul: A supplier code of conduct with clauses on ethics, product safety, worker welfare, human rights and environment.
A right for the buyer to audit or send questionnaires.
Data requests that follow from the buyer's own BRSR, such as energy, emissions, water and waste figures.
Worker safety and wellbeing, Principle 3: ISO 45001, which replaced OHSAS 18001.
Labour and human rights, Principles 3 and 5: SA 8000.
Sustainable sourcing, Principle 2: FSC, Rainforest Alliance, Fairtrade or Trustea, depending on your material.

sections.h: If you cannot meet every clause yet
p: Do not tick every box. Sign with a short written note of the gaps and dates to close them. A buyer can work with a dated plan; a false yes found in an audit ends the relationship.

senseible: When the code of conduct asks for your energy and emissions, Senseible prepares Scope 1 and 2 figures from your electricity bills and fuel invoices, with each line linked to its bill, ready to send to the buyer.
